title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: E/S is an elliptic curve over a base with 2 invertible. The previous page treats the universal Legendre curve y^2 = x(x-1)(x-λ) over U_{0,3} × μ_4^*, where U_{0,3} = P^1 − {0,1,∞} and μ_4^* is the scheme of primitive 4th roots of unity. There Grothendieck identified a canonical bundle Δ_E with O_{U_{0,3}}(1)^♮, using the fact that over μ_4^* the conic bundle Q_{0S} is trivial.

On this page he works with an arbitrary E/S.

(1) A 'Legendre epi-rigidification' is an isomorphism K: Δ_{E/S} ≅ O_Σ(1)_t^♮. Here Σ is the reference P^1 with its marked points and t a tangential datum. These isomorphisms are the sections of a torsor L_{E/S} under μ_{4,S}, called 'le torseur des épi-rigidifications de Legendre de E/S'. The action is by scalar multiplication through μ_4 ⊂ G_m.

(2) He then gives a second description that uses only the untwisted O_Σ(1)_t, not O_Σ(1)_t^♮. Consider isomorphisms K': Δ_{E/S} ≅ O_Σ(1)_t, formula (40). Their square K'^{⊗2} is read as an isomorphism T_{Σ,t} ≅ T_{Σ,t} ∧^{{±1}} ω_J, formula (41). This is the tangent line twisted by the μ_2-torsor ω_J; ω_J is apparently a Jacobi-type square-root torsor attached to E. One requires that K'^{⊗2} come from a section of ω_J. These K' form a μ_4-torsor Q_{E/S}.

(3) The next page completes the picture:
- Q_{E/S}/μ_2 ≅ ω_J, formula (42).
- There is a canonical isomorphism of μ_4-torsors relating L_{E/S} to Q_{E/S} and the reference conic torsor Q_{0S}, formula (43); it is written there both as Q_{E/S} ∧ Q_{0S} and as Isom(Q_{0S}^{-1}, Q_{E/S}).
- The μ_2-torsor induced from L is canonical: L/μ_2 ≅ μ_4^* ∧ ω_J, formula (44).
- All this is compared with 'Jacobi epi-glyphs of order 4' (Jacobi quartic, i.e. level-4 type normalizations).

Purpose: to pin down exactly how much extra data beyond a level-2 structure is needed to put E in Legendre form. The answer is a μ_4-torsor, and its μ_2-part is the quadratic-twist torsor. The aim is to describe the Legendre stack and the actions of the relevant symmetry groups on U_{0,3} × μ_4^* and on Δ. This is part of Grothendieck's program of explicit 'modular' rigidifications in genus 1 relating M_{1,1}[2] to M_{0,4} = U_{0,3}, in the spirit of the Esquisse's Teichmüller tower.
errors: No clear mathematical error is visible, but the objects (Δ_{E/S}, the ♮-twist, Σ, the tangential index t, ω_J) are not defined on this page, so the claims cannot be fully checked.

The orientation/inverse convention in the comparison L_{E/S} versus Q_{E/S} and Q_{0S} (next page: Q∧Q_0 written alongside Isom(Q_0^{-1}, Q)) is somewhat ambiguous. This is harmless for torsors under the commutative group μ_4, but the notation is inconsistent.

ideas.what: Legendre normal form data as a μ_4-torsor ('épi-rigidifications de Legendre') attached to any elliptic curve E/S in characteristic ≠ 2
ideas.modern_name: Legendre level structure / rigidification of M(2) over U_{0,3}; the moduli of Legendre-form curves as a μ_4-torsor over the level-2 stack
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Legendre, Jacobi); in moduli form Igusa, Deligne–Rapoport, Katz–Mazur (Legendre family over Z[1/2,λ,1/(λ(1-λ))])

ideas.what: Alternative description via K': Δ ≅ O_Σ(1)_t whose square comes from a section of a μ_2-torsor ω_J twisting the tangent line at a tangential base point; Q_{E/S}/μ_2 ≅ ω_J
ideas.modern_name: Square-root (μ_4 over μ_2) torsor; quadratic-twist torsor of an elliptic curve with level-2 structure; tangential base points on P^1−{0,1,∞}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tangential base points: Deligne (1989); quadratic twist torsors are standard

ideas.what: Comparison L_{E/S} ≅ Q_{E/S} contracted with the reference conic torsor Q_{0S}, trivial over μ_4^*
ideas.modern_name: Contracted product of torsors; triviality of the Brauer–Severi conic over μ_4^* (i.e. once √−1 is adjoined)

missed.claim: An explicit functorial μ_4-torsor description of 'Legendre epi-rigidifications' for an arbitrary elliptic curve over a base where 2 is invertible. It splits into a μ_2-part (the canonical quadratic-twist torsor ω_J) and a conic part (Q_{0S}) that trivializes over μ_4^*. This is a careful stack-theoretic account of why the Legendre family lives naturally over U_{0,3} × μ_4^*, and of how it compares with Jacobi order-4 normalizations. The standard literature usually just states M(2) ≅ U_{0,3} × Bμ_2 over Z[1/2] without this tangential-base-point and μ_4 bookkeeping.
missed.quote: les épi-rigidifications de Legendre K : Δ_{E/S} ≃ O_Σ(1)_t^♮ forment les sections d'un torseur sous μ_{4S}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The arithmetic of the Legendre family is used in work on Galois actions on π_1 of P^1−{0,1,∞} and on M_{1,1}, e.g. Nakamura's and Hain's work on the elliptic Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory. For that work, a precise description of the μ_4 / √−1 ambiguity and of the tangential normalizations is useful, though probably reconstructible by experts.

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful, Grothendieck-style torsor bookkeeping for Legendre normal forms, with idiosyncratic terminology ('épi-rigidification', 'épi-glyphe'). The underlying mathematics (Legendre family, level-2 and level-4 structures, quadratic twists, the μ_4 ambiguity) is well known. The presentation is unpublished, but it holds no result a specialist would find genuinely new.
transcription_corrections: The group written 'M_4' / 'H_4' is almost certainly μ_4 (blackboard μ), with μ_2 its quotient under squaring; read μ_{4S} throughout.
'Dans [-par la-] {+ma+} direction en torseur ainsi de [?]' should read roughly 'Donnons une description du torseur ainsi défini de la façon suivante'.
'Construction de torseur par multiplication scalaire de μ_4 ⊂ (G_m...)': the parenthesis likely refers to G_m.
'ω_∃' should be ω_J (matching the next page's ω_J), with the subscript {±1} under the contracted product: T_{Σ,t} ∧^{{±1}} ω_J.
The first line is likely 'Considérons une courbe elliptique [...] relative E/S' rather than 'semi-valution'.
'(évidemment unique)' sits under formula (41) and refers to the interpretation of K'^{⊗2}.
The last line likely reads 'qu'on peut interpréter comme le schéma des [racines/sommets] d'un ...' and continues on the next page; it is uncertain.
